summary: Defines how a WebRTC data channel is used to carry CLUE protocol messages between two CLUE entities. This gives telepresence endpoints a reliable path for their control messages alongside the media. It is an experimental document.

plainLanguage.summary: The CLUE data channel is the path that carries the CLUE messages between two devices in a call. It is built on the WebRTC data channel, which runs inside an encrypted DTLS connection, and it delivers every message reliably and in order.

subtitle: The path that carries CLUE messages between two telepresence devices.

tldr.problem: The CLUE protocol needs a reliable, ordered path between the two ends of a telepresence call, and that path has to be described in the session description so that both ends agree on it.
tldr.mechanism: The CLUE data channel is built on the WebRTC data channel mechanism, which is a pair of SCTP streams over an SCTP association carried inside a DTLS connection. The RFC fixes the SCTP options used, including reliable ordered delivery and the payload protocol identifier 51, and defines the SDP lines that describe the channel.
tldr.outcome: The channel gives the CLUE protocol a transport that delivers every message in order and can be closed on its own without affecting other data channels on the same association. The document is Experimental.

today: RFC 8850 is an Experimental document and has not been obsoleted. It is the companion to RFC 8848, which describes how a CLUE session is signalled, and to RFC 8847, which defines the CLUE protocol that the channel carries.

sections.title: What the CLUE Data Channel Is
sections.content:
The CLUE data channel carries the CLUE protocol messages between two CLUE entities. It is built on the WebRTC data channel mechanism, so it is a pair of SCTP streams over a single SCTPoDTLS association, which is an SCTP association carried over a DTLS connection. A CLUE entity is a SIP user agent that supports the CLUE data channel and the CLUE protocol, and a CLUE session is a SIP session between two user agents in which such a channel has been established.

The RFC also defines how the association is described in the Session Description Protocol (SDP), and how the SDP-based data channel negotiation mechanism is used to create the channel. The details of the CLUE protocol itself, and the offer and answer procedures for negotiating a CLUE session, are outside the scope of this document. So is the use of the Data Channel Establishment Protocol.

Two rules from the WebRTC data channel mechanism apply here. Both SCTP streams that make up the channel must belong to the same association, and both must use the same stream identifier. Within a given CLUE session, a CLUE entity must use a single CLUE data channel for all the CLUE messages it sends to its peer.
sections.plainLanguage: The CLUE data channel is the path that carries the CLUE messages between two devices in a call. It is built on the WebRTC data channel, which runs inside an encrypted DTLS connection.

sections.title: SCTP Settings for the Channel
sections.content:
Several SCTP options are fixed for a CLUE data channel.

A CLUE entity must use the payload protocol identifier 51 when sending a CLUE message. That value says the message holds data encoded in UTF-8. It does not say which application protocol the message belongs to.

The channel is reliable and ordered. The WebRTC data channel mechanism requires support for the partial reliability extension and for the limited retransmission policy, but a CLUE entity must not use them, because CLUE messages are required to always be sent reliably. If an entity detects that the peer uses either extension, it must terminate the session. The entity must also use the ordered delivery service of SCTP, so that messages are delivered in the order they were sent.

The entity must support the stream reset extension, and the dynamic address reconfiguration parameter of SCTP must be used to signal that support. The other features of that parameter must not be used for CLUE data channels. SCTP multihoming is not supported for an SCTPoDTLS association, so it cannot be used for a CLUE data channel either.

Closing the channel means sending an SCTP reset message on the outgoing stream of the channel. When the peer receives it, it also sends a reset message on its own outgoing stream, unless it has already done so. The association, and any other data channels established on the same association, are not affected by those reset messages.
sections.plainLanguage: CLUE messages must arrive, and they must arrive in the order they were sent, so the channel is set to reliable and ordered delivery. The data is marked as UTF-8 text, and the channel can be closed on its own without disturbing anything else sharing the connection.

sections.title: Describing the Channel in SDP
sections.content:
The media line for the association carries the media type application, a port, a protocol name and the format webrtc-datachannel. The protocol name is either UDP/DTLS/SCTP or TCP/DTLS/SCTP. Entities should not use the TCP form unless it is known that UDP will not work, for instance when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment mechanism determines that TCP transport is required. The sctp-port attribute carries the SCTP port of the association, and the entity may choose any valid value.

The dcmap attribute describes the channels carried on the association. For a CLUE data channel, the stream identifier is the value of the SCTP stream used to realise the channel, the subprotocol is CLUE, the label is application specific, and the ordered flag is true. The max-retr and max-time parameters are not used, because the channel is always reliable and ordered. The dcsa attribute is not used at all when establishing a CLUE data channel.

The RFC's own example is short: an application line on port 54111 using UDP/DTLS/SCTP, an sctp-port of 5000, and a dcmap line naming stream 2 with the CLUE subprotocol and ordered delivery set.
sections.plainLanguage: The session description lists the data channel like any other media line. It names the protocol, the port and the SCTP port, and a dcmap line records the stream number, the CLUE subprotocol name and that delivery is ordered.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The specification relies on the security properties of the WebRTC data channel described in RFC 8831, including the reliance on DTLS. Because CLUE sessions are established using SIP and SDP, protecting the data channel against message modification and recovery also requires the SIP authentication and authorization mechanisms described in RFC 3261, used for session establishment before the data channel is established.
sections.plainLanguage: The channel relies on DTLS for its security. Because the session is set up with SIP, the SIP authentication and authorization mechanisms must also be used before the channel is established.
